interactions.summary: The class extends Jiang's art exercise by naming several modes of engagement: taking the artist's point of view, connecting the work to oneself, focusing on details, world-building, and recovering the message or story.

claims.claim: Jiang accepts technical analysis and perspective-switching as part of art's effect: viewers do not just receive the image but move between the artist's position and their own.
Jiang labels close attention to parts of the painting as world-building: the viewer moves from the whole toward each component in order to animate the depicted reality.
Another accepted mechanism is interpretive recovery of message and story: viewers try to understand what the artist wanted to convey, not just what is optically present.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang's preferred name for detail-work is world-building: the viewer makes the pictured world denser by entering its parts.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives the imagination thesis a concrete operative verb rather than leaving it as vague appreciation.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang uses world-building to describe the viewer's effort to fill out each part of a painting until its implied reality becomes more fully inhabited.

chronology_notes.note: The lecture is broadening its account of imagination from simple participation to a toolkit of analysis, perspective-shifting, detail work, and message recovery.
